beats.text: Part 4 of this course asked one kind of question fifteen times: where is it stored, what reads it, and what happens when it is stale or missing? Gate 5, the mastery test for this part, asks the same question, and it asks it of you with no book open.

beats.text: Every gate has 100 points in four parts with fixed weights. Part 1, Concepts: 30 points, six written questions of 5 points each, closed book, no terminal. Each requires a mechanism: which objects, refs, files or rules are involved, and what reads or writes them.

beats.text: The pass rule has two conditions. The threshold overall, 85 here, and at least 70 percent in every part: 21 of 30 in Concepts, 14 of 20 in Prediction, 21 of 30 in Hands-on, 14 of 20 in Oral. A total above the threshold with one part below 70 percent is a miss.

beats.text: Try it on the pack index, the lookup file beside a pack. It stores object IDs with offsets into a pack. Every object lookup reads it. It can't be stale, since a pack never changes. If it's missing, Git warns, and you rebuild it from the pack, because it's derived data.
beats.tele: Try it on the pack index, the lookup file beside a pack. It stores object IDs with offsets into a pack. Every object lookup reads it. It can't be stale, since a pack never changes. If it's missing, Git warns, and you rebuild it from the pack, because it's derived data.

beats.text: Try it on the commit-graph. It stores parents, generation numbers and changed-path filters. History walks and path-limited logs read it. Stale: slower, not wrong. Missing: Git reads the objects.
beats.tele: Try it on the commit-graph. It stores parents, generation numbers and changed-path filters. History walks and path-limited logs read it. Stale: slower, not wrong. Missing: Git reads the objects.

beats.text: It is the broadest question of the part, and it has a follow-up about why four hundred versions of a large line-oriented file are not four hundred copies on disk, and when that argument fails. A strong answer is layered: objects and how they are named, then how they are stored loose and in packs, then names, then the index. It keeps the object level and the storage level apart, and it knows the limits of delta compression. Give it in two minutes, then give it in thirty seconds.
